bull_bear.body:
- **Interim dividend INR12/share** (record date 17-Jul-26, pay 27-Jul-26); LTM dividend **INR60/share = 93.2% payout** of net income. (Prior-year board policy: return ≥75% of net income.)
- AI-datacenter capex **explicitly ring-fenced from the payout policy**; funded via FCF + partner/debt mix, disciplined and staged.
- Acquisitions: Jaspersoft (completed), CTG (pending), Sarvam ($150M strategic stake).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Two large US telcos** — sharp discretionary-spend cuts; already flagged last quarter, now playing through ERS (Tech/Telecom/Media) in subsequent quarters.
- **Healthcare / Life Sciences** — structural drag: off a ~$500M run-rate, gradual decline over 8–9 quarters; medical-device regulatory work ended and wasn't refilled; US healthcare sector "heavily stressed" (most of the vertical's revenue is US).
- **AI price deflation** — AI-disrupted/commoditised services being optimised away; TCV-per-deal pressure; token-cost economics (costs may fall but total token consumption/cost rises → need economic tiered/SLM model).
- **Datacenter execution / tenancy risk** — analyst pushback on ROIC/tenancy if the compute-demand cycle turns (100GW of announced AI-DC pipeline; SpaceX/Meta leasing compute); mgmt counters market is "heavily GPU-starved," 50MW is a tiny fraction of need.
- **Guidance conservatism** — held 1–4% despite record bookings; macro unchanged since March; directional update only after Q2.
- **New Labor Code** one-time EPS impact; DSO up 2 days.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident and specific on AI strategy (five pillars, named deals, hard AI-revenue numbers); disciplined on capital ("won't correlate INR3,500cr with 50MW," FCF-gated, payout-protected).
- Transparent on idiosyncratic weakness (named two-telco cuts, healthcare structural drag) rather than glossing.
- Pragmatic on guidance — deliberately conservative given only one quarter in and unchanged macro; measured on mega-deal contribution timing (Apr-2027 steady state).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The AI-datacenter move is a **business-model inflection** — a services company building infrastructure, which mgmt frames as a *reversal* of the cloud/digital cycle (then you partnered hyperscalers; now private/sovereign SLM stacks require owning the full stack). Watch capital discipline vs. scope creep toward 50MW.
- "Megawatt is the anchor, not the product" — the DC play is really a **wrapper to lock in high-margin managed-services/outcome-based contracts** and internal consumption, not a colo/capacity land-grab.
- Sovereign-AI/SLM thesis reframes AI deflation as an **engineering-services tailwind** (data work + model training per client) rather than a pure headwind.
- Record Q1 bookings + a separately-announced mega deal, yet guidance untouched — signals mgmt sees near-term revenue governed by seasonality/give-backs and the telco/healthcare drag, not order intake.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **ITBS**: flat QoQ, +4.2% YoY — resilient despite two-telco headwind + SAP program.
- **ERS**: −3.7% QoQ, +0.3% YoY — decline concentrated in **Tech and Telecom, Media & Entertainment**; sharp discretionary cuts in two large US telcos + high tech base.
- **HCL Software**: $313M, +2.2% QoQ / −5.3% YoY; ARR $1.063B (+2% YoY). Jaspersoft adds the visualization layer to data portfolio (DataConnect, Ingres, Informix, Zen, VectorAI DB, Data Intelligence/Observability).
- **Advanced AI**: $171M, +10.6% QoQ / +62.1% YoY.
- **Geographies (YoY)**: USA +2.9%, Europe +0.1%, RoW +10.8%, India +16.9%.
- **Verticals**: 6 of 7 grew YoY; led by **Public Services +12%** and **Retail & CPG +10.1%**; BFSI strong (~12 quarters of momentum, highest-in-industry YoY). Weak: Telecom, High-tech, Life Sciences/Healthcare.
- **Clients added (YoY)**: +1 in $100M, +6 in $50M, +11 in $20M, +31 in $10M.
- **People**: 223,889 (−3,292 QoQ); attrition 12.7% LTM; revenue/employee +3.3% YoY (up 5 straight quarters).

- Reported EBIT margin walk QoQ (JFM'26 16.5% → AMJ'26 16.9%, +39bps): **+70bps** lower restructuring, **+20bps** PDD benefit, **+60bps** forex; **−110bps** seasonality (annual productivity give-backs + ERS decline).

outlook.body:
- **FY27 revenue growth: retained 1–4% CC** — organic, **excludes acquisitions (incl. Jaspersoft, CTG)**.
- **FY27 EBIT margin: 17.5–18.5%** — organic; **includes ~40–50bps restructuring-cost impact**. Acquisition revenue/margin sits on top of (outside) the guide.
- Guidance held despite record Q1 bookings — mgmt wants to "see how things pan out next quarter"; will revisit directional change after Q2.
- **Mega deal** (Fortune Global 50, Europe) signed early July → NOT in Q1; transition starts in ~2 months, **steady state only Apr-2027 → negligible FY27 revenue impact**.
- **Jaspersoft**: ~**$10–15M/quarter** contribution from Q2 (seasonality-affected), outside guidance.
- **CTG**: expected to close later part of this (Q2) quarter, outside guidance.
- Margin recovery to old **18–19% band**: deferred — will give FY28 guidance "at an appropriate time" next year.

outlook.body:
- **Net-new TCV $2.4B**, "highest-ever Q1 bookings"; well-balanced across verticals / service lines / geographies. Excludes the July mega deal.
- **Mega deal** (post-Q1): Europe-HQ Fortune Global 50 firm — technology partner for AI-led transformation of digital workplace + enterprise networks (AI Force platform, software-defined solutions, digital employee experience).
- **AI Factory**: global technology major expanded partnership, **incremental scope >$180M** for AI datacenter build-out (latest GPU tech, LLM training).
- **Fortune 250 semiconductor-equipment OEM**: SAP-enabled design-to-manufacturing, SAP + PLM + MES integration.
- Europe automotive OEM: AI-led SRE transformation (AI Force). Europe manufacturer: physical-AI navigation stack for autonomous robot. Indian research org: secure chip / trusted-computing silicon.
- Pipeline described "healthy"; encouraged by potential Q2 bookings. AI Labs crossed **1,000+ AI engagements** in Q1.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **AI-native + AI-amplified** services: fastest-growing enterprise-spend pool — the intended disproportionate beneficiary; **AI-disrupted (commoditized) work** to be optimised/deflated faster than the market.
- **AI Datacenter business (NEW growth vector)** — see §8. Full-stack (design + DevOps + cloud ops + software), not colo; anchors managed-services / outcome-based contracts.
- **Sovereign AI-as-a-service / SLMs**: zero-trust + tiered architecture (Tier-1 private on-prem/VPC SLMs fine-tuned on enterprise data; Tier-2 frontier models via policy-enforcing inferencing gateway). $150M strategic investment in **Sarvam** opens Indian sovereign-AI market; SLM-training = "another engineering-services wave."
- **AI IP / platforms**: AI Force 2.2 (VS Code plugin, multimodal, long-term memory, AWS-native), Agent Store, AI Force for Oracle; deployed across **92 client accounts**; **23 industry AI solutions**.
- **Partnerships**: Red Hat (AI Factory), Google Cloud (dedicated Gemini enterprise BU + autonomous finance platform), Intel + Google Cloud AI Innovation Zones (Santa Clara, Chennai), OpenAI Trusted Access for Cyber, AWS AI Services Competency, Dell/HPE partner-of-the-year, MetLife Stadium AI partner (FIFA 2026 final venue).

deepdive.thesis: HCLTech opened FY27 with a seasonally-weak-but-resilient Q1 (revenue $3,650M, −0.5% QoQ / +2.6% YoY CC; margin 16.9%, +39bps QoQ) carried by record Q1 bookings ($2.4B net-new TCV, highest-ever Q1) and Advanced AI ($171M, +62% YoY). The headline event is a strategic pivot into the **AI-datacenter/full-stack sovereign-AI business** — an initial INR3,500cr investment scaling toward a 50MW ambition — funded off FCF/partners without touching the 75%+ payout policy. FY27 guidance held at 1–4% CC / 17.5–18.5% EBIT despite two US-telco discretionary cuts and a structural healthcare-vertical drag.

risks.note: The BRSR reports a workforce of 237,098 (227,181 permanent) and voluntary attrition (LTM - IT Services) of 12.51% for permanent employees in FY26 against 12.99% in FY25 and 12.42% in FY24. HCLTech owns no plants or manufacturing facilities, so capacity is entirely people; sustained double-digit churn in a business selling billable skills is a structural cost and delivery-continuity risk, aggravated by the need to re-skill the base for AI, automation, cybersecurity and cloud.
risks.risk: People-dependent delivery model exposed to attrition and wage/skill inflation

risks.note: 100% of turnover comes from one activity - computer programming, consultancy, software and related activities (GICS Information Technology - Software and Services). Within that, IT & Business Services contributes 74% of turnover, Engineering and R&D Services 17% and HCLSoftware 9%. There is no diversifying business line, so any downturn in enterprise IT services demand or in the ITBS segment flows almost fully to the top line.
risks.risk: Revenue concentrated in a single business activity and one dominant segment

risks.note: The BRSR states exports contribute 91.54% of total turnover for the standalone entity, with markets across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. Revenue is therefore earned largely in foreign currency against a substantially INR/offshore cost base, exposing reported earnings to exchange-rate movement and to demand, immigration and trade policy in a small number of overseas markets.
risks.risk: Export and currency concentration - over nine-tenths of standalone turnover is exported

risks.note: The Company positions itself as a preferred digital and AI partner to Global 2000 companies, Global 2000 equivalent organizations and emerging enterprises, and states that its strategy 'emphasizes building deep, strategic client relationships as a trusted long-term partner'. That deep-few model concentrates revenue in large accounts, so the loss, insourcing or budget cut of a top relationship is disproportionately material.
risks.risk: Client concentration in a narrow set of very large enterprise accounts

risks.note: Clients are concentrated in Financial Services, Manufacturing, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Technology and Services, Public Services (Energy & Utilities, Travel-Transport-Logistics and Government), Retail and CPG, and Telecommunications, Media, Publishing and Entertainment. Serving regulated and government customers imports their data-protection, security and procurement obligations into HCLTech's delivery, raising the cost of failure on any engagement.
risks.risk: Exposure to heavily regulated client verticals and their compliance regimes

risks.note: As on March 31, 2026 the Company had 125 subsidiaries and 3 associate companies, with new entities incorporated in Austria (HCL Technologies Holdings GmbH) and the UAE (HCL Technologies Middle East LLC) during the year. The Directors' Report acknowledges the burden directly, noting that restructuring is done 'after taking into consideration the business aspects, local laws and regulations' in order to reduce the number of entities - i.e. a standing compliance, tax and administrative-cost overhead across many jurisdictions.

FY26 saw two acquisitions (Wobby BV, an Agentic AI software startup in Belgium, via Actian Germany GmbH; and Finergic Solutions Pte. Ltd. of Singapore, core banking and wealth-management transformation, via HCL Singapore Pte Ltd, completed March 6, 2026, pulling in Finergic Consulting Pte. Ltd. and Finergic Luxembourg S.A.) alongside five entities merged, liquidated or de-registered - including the liquidation of the CeleritiFinTech Limited joint venture on October 28, 2025. Continuous inorganic capability-buying and entity unwinding carries integration, retention and value-realisation risk.
risks.risk: Acquisition, integration and portfolio-churn execution risk

risks.note: Risk oversight rests on a Board Risk Management Committee (one of six Board Committees), a Risk Management Policy 'that ensures appropriate management of risks in line with its internal systems and culture', and internal financial controls designed for 'safeguarding of assets from unauthorized use & prevention and detection of frauds & errors'. The Directors' Report itself carries no risk enumeration - it defers the detailed Risk Management section to the MD&A - so investors depend on the effectiveness of that framework, and on the auditors' clean report and no-fraud statement, for assurance.
risks.risk: Reliance on the internal control, ethics and risk-policy framework rather than a disclosed enterprise risk register
